sentences.text: In the instant case the prosecution is alleging that the accused being the driver of the Jeep drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to Scooter due to which the rider sustained injuries and later succumbed to death.
The prosecution contended that accused committed the offences punishable U/s.279 & 304(A) of IPC.

Section 279 IPC deals with rash and negligent driving of any vehicle or riding on a public way in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life or likely to cause hurt or injury to any person.

In order to constitute an offence U/s.279 of IPC, it must be established that the accused was driving the vehicle on a public way in rash and negligent manner to endanger human life or to likely cause to hurt or injury to any other person.
For the purpose of section 279 rash and negligent may be described as criminal rashness or criminal negligence.
It must be more than mere carelessness of error of judgment.

The essential ingredients of section 279 are: (1) rash and negligent driving or riding on a public way, (ii) The act must be such as to endanger human life or likely to cause hurt or injury to any person.

24. In order to constitute offence U/s.304(a) of IPC the prosecution must establish the essential ingredients of Sec.304(A) of IPC which are as follows: (I) The death of the C.C.No.89/2022 person must be in question (ii) The death must have caused by the accused; and (iii) The act of the accused was rash or negligent and it did not amount to culpable homicide.

25. He contended his vehicle has not dashed to deceased vehicle as contended by the prosecution.

sentences.text: 29. The burden is upon the prosecution to establish that the accused being the driver of bus drove his vehicle in rash and negligent manner.

To bring home the culpability of accused under section 279 and 304(A) IPC, it is necessary to know the relevant provisions of law which reads as follows:
Section 279. Rash driving or riding on a public way:
C.C.No.89/2022 Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
In the case on hand P.W.2 and 3 claims the accused drove his vehicle in high speed and caused accident.

Whether high speed alone constitutes negligence Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case titled "State of Karnataka Vs. Satish ((1998) 8 SCC 493)" wherein the Apex Court observed: "merely because the truck was being driven at a high speed does not bespeak of either "negligence or rashness" by itself.

entities.text: State of Karnataka Vs. Satish ((1998) 8 SCC 493)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: None of the witness examined by the prosecution could give any indication, even approximately, as to what they meant by "high speed".
High speed is a relative term.
It was for the prosecution to bring on record material to establish as to what it meant by high speed in the facts and circumstances of the case.

In a criminal trial, the burden of providing everything essential to the establishment of the charge against an accused always rests on the prosecution and there is a presumption of innocence in favour of the accused until the contrary is proved.
Criminality is not to be presumed subject of course to some statutory exceptions.
There is no statutory exception pleaded in the present case.
In the absence of any material on record, no presumption of C.C.No.89/2022 rashness or negligence could be drawn by invoking the maxim "res ipsa loquitur".
Mere fact that an innocent died in a road accident cannot be a reason to raise any presumption of rashness and negligence in absence of any other cogent evidence.
30. Prosecution contended accused drove his vehicle in high speed in negligent manner and dashed to two wheeler which was proceeding in the said road.
Upon perusal of the sketch map as per Ex.P.12 the accident has taken place exactly in the center of the road and it is main road.
Prosecution claims accused drove towards right side and dashed to bike of the deceased .
In the case on hand since the accident has taken place in the main road the version of the eye witness that accused dashed to rear side of the bike appears doubtful.
It cannot be brushed out completely that the deceased came in high speed and dashed to proceeding bus in the main road.
The impact of accident clearly supports the said contention and the front portion of the two wheeler was completely damaged.
If vehicle was dashed from rear side the chances of damaging in front side is quite not possible.
The contention of the accused the deceased came in high speed and dashed to accused vehicle appears true.

Here prosecution has to establish the negligent act on the part of the Rajajinagar Trps vs Chandrashekar B N on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54501653/

sentences.text:
With regard to negligent act the Hon'ble Apex court in "Mohammed Aynuddin @ Miyan vs State of Andhra C.C.No.89/2022 Pradesh reported in 2000 SCC(CRI) 1281, wherein the Court discussed in detail the constituents of a "rash or negligent act" and observed:
"A rash act is primarily an over hasty act.

entities.text: Mohammed Aynuddin @ Miyan vs State of Andhra C.C.No.89/2022 Pradesh reported in 2000 SCC(CRI) 1281
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is opposed to a deliberate act.
Still a rash act can be a deliberate act in the sense that it was done without due care and caution.
Culpable rashness lies in running the risk of doing an act with recklessness and with indifference as to the consequences.
Criminal negligence is the failure to exercise duty with reasonable and proper care and precaution guarding against injury to the public generally or to any individual in particular.

It is the imperative duty of the driver of a vehicle to adopt such reasonable and proper care and precaution."
31.
The witnesses have not stated rash and negligent act on the part of the accused on the date of alleged incident.

Further eye witnesses have not stated the rash and negligent act of the accused to show accused drove his vehicle in negligent manner, the burden is upon the prosecution to establish the same but they failed to establish same.
Therefore, in this circumstance of the case, the case of prosecution regarding rash and negligent act of accused could not be made out beyond reasonable doubt.
32. Therefore, looking to the evidence available on record and the materials placed by way of oral and exhibits, the case of prosecution appears to be doubtful.
There is doubt as to whether the accused has driven his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger the human life and C.C.No.89/2022 personal safety of others.
Therefore, in the circumstances of the case, the prosecution has failed to prove the alleged offence against the accused.
Accordingly, the points under consideration are answered point No.1 and 2 IN THE NEGATIVE.
33. POINT No.3:

In view of the above discussions and findings I proceed to pass the following ORDER Acting U/sec. 255(1) of Criminal procedure code, the accused is hereby acquitted of the offences alleged against him punishable U/sec. 279 and 304(A) of IPC.
Bail bonds of accused and surety bonds shall stand canceled after completion of appeal period.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Around 6:00 PM, a speeding Eicher mini bus bearing number KA-52-B-0791, while overtaking in front of the FTI compound, hit his bike.
Section 279 IPC deals with rash and negligent driving of any vehicle or riding on a public way in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life or likely to cause hurt or injury to any person.
In order to constitute an offence U/s.279 of IPC, it must be established that the accused was driving the vehicle on a public way in rash and negligent manner to endanger human life or to likely cause to hurt or injury to any other person.
For the purpose of section 279 rash and negligent may be described as criminal rashness or criminal negligence.
It must be more than mere carelessness of error of judgment.
The essential ingredients of section 279 are: (1) rash and negligent driving or riding on a public way, (ii) The act must be such as to endanger human life or likely to cause hurt or injury to any person.
24. In order to constitute offence U/s.304(a) of IPC the prosecution must establish the essential ingredients of Sec.304(A) of IPC which are as follows: (I) The death of the C.C.No.89/2022 person must be in question (ii) The death must have caused by the accused; and (iii) The act of the accused was rash or negligent and it did not amount to culpable homicide.
29. The burden is upon the prosecution to establish that the accused being the driver of bus drove his vehicle in rash and negligent manner.
In a criminal trial, the burden of providing everything essential to the establishment of the charge against an accused always rests on the prosecution and there is a presumption of innocence in favour of the accused until the contrary is proved.
Criminality is not to be presumed subject of course to some statutory exceptions.
There is no statutory exception pleaded in the present case.
In the absence of any material on record, no presumption of C.C.No.89/2022 rashness or negligence could be drawn by invoking the maxim "res ipsa loquitur".
Mere fact that an innocent died in a road accident cannot be a reason to raise any presumption of rashness and negligence in absence of any other cogent evidence.
It cannot be brushed out completely that the deceased came in high speed and dashed to proceeding bus in the main road.
If vehicle was dashed from rear side the chances of damaging in front side is quite not possible.
Here prosecution has to establish the negligent act on the part of the Rajajinagar Trps vs Chandrashekar B N on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54501653/
8 accused.
The witnesses have not stated rash and negligent act on the part of the accused on the date of alleged incident.
Further eye witnesses have not stated the rash and negligent act of the accused to show accused drove his vehicle in negligent manner, the burden is upon the prosecution to establish the same but they failed to establish same.
Therefore, in this circumstance of the case, the case of prosecution regarding rash and negligent act of accused could not be made out beyond reasonable doubt.
32. Therefore, looking to the evidence available on record and the materials placed by way of oral and exhibits, the case of prosecution appears to be doubtful.
There is doubt as to whether the accused has driven his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger the human life and C.C.No.89/2022 personal safety of others.
Therefore, in the circumstances of the case, the prosecution has failed to prove the alleged offence against the accused.
